The '''2006–07 Bundesliga''' was the 44th season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier football league. It began on 11 August 2006 and ended on 19 May 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co12/se580/all-matches/ |title=Bundesliga 2006/2007 » Schedule |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref> [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] were the defending champions.

==Team changes from 2005–06==
Three teams from the [[2. Bundesliga]] were promoted at the end of previous season: 
* [[VfL Bochum]] (champions)
* [[Alemannia Aachen]] (runners-up)
* [[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]]

The three teams relegated were:
* [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]]
* [[1. FC Köln]]
* [[MSV Duisburg]]

== Season overview ==
[[VfB Stuttgart]] began the campaign with the youngest squad of the Bundesliga and were widely seen as a competitor for a [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] berth. They began their season with a 0–3 home defeat against [[1. FC Nürnberg]] and even dropped in reach of the relegation zone after another home defeat against [[Borussia Dortmund]] during the third round.

During the rest of the season the team managed to stabilize in the upper third of the table, eventually winning the last eight games of the season while competitors [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]], [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] struggled. Stuttgart went on to claim their third championship in the Bundesliga and fifth [[German champions (football)|German championship]] overall with a 2–1 home victory against [[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]] during the last round of the season.

One week after winning the league championship, Stuttgart failed to win [[Double (association football)|the Double]] after losing the [[2007 DFB-Pokal Final]] against Nürnberg with a score of 2–3.

Manager [[Armin Veh]] who claimed his first championship as a Bundesliga coach was elected [[German Football Manager of the Year]], while [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]] [[Mario Gómez]] was named [[Footballer of the Year (Germany)]] in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/mario-gomez-10-things-vfb-stuttgart-world-cup-bayern-munich-besiktas-479947.jsp|title=Mario Gomez: 10 things on the VfB Stuttgart star|access-date=2019-01-27|archive-date=27 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200527063334/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/mario-gomez-10-things-vfb-stuttgart-world-cup-bayern-munich-besiktas-479947.jsp|url-status=dead}}</ref>
